briefing: Trump's envoys are heading to Moscow and Kyiv this weekend with a plan to end the Ukraine war, though talks have stalled; separately, Trump claims Putin has no intention of attacking NATO territory.
US employment data came in three times stronger than expected in August, opening the door to higher interest rates—contrary to Trump's recent threats to halt trade unless the Fed cuts rates.
Russia is suspected of orchestrating a spiralling sabotage campaign across Europe, including an attack on Leipzig airport, signalling escalating hybrid warfare.
Italian PM Meloni claims Italy has regained stability and is no longer Europe's problem case, asserting her government retains strong public support.
France arrested three suspects planning violent action against the Jewish community; separately, the National Rally and UK Reform party signed a pact on clandestine immigration.

August jobs report beat expectations (162K added), keeping Fed rate-hike debate open for September meeting; this macro uncertainty is driving Bitcoin's refuge-asset appeal but pressuring equities and your financial sector holdings.
